projects.title: Write your workshop tools
projects.description: Write small programs that calculate job costs, clean text and handle work notes.

tasks.title: Build a labour estimate
tasks.prompt: A repair costs hours × rate plus callout. Calculate the labour subtotal before adding the callout fee. Assign the final amount to result.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: Follow which values each assignment needs.
The callout fee is added once, after the hourly calculation.
tasks.correction: Keep the fixed callout fee outside the multiplication by hours.
tasks.solution:
subtotal = hours * rate
result = subtotal + callout
tasks.explanation: The hourly subtotal depends on hours and rate. Adding callout afterwards charges the fixed fee once.

tasks.title: Pack complete boxes
tasks.prompt: items must fit into boxes of capacity. Assign result a dictionary with boxes for the number of full boxes and left for the remaining items.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: Separate the whole-box count from the remainder.
For nonnegative items, // gives the full-box count and % gives the leftover count.
tasks.correction: Ordinary division can return a fraction of a box. The task asks for whole boxes and a separate remainder.
tasks.solution: result = {'boxes': items // capacity, 'left': items % capacity}
tasks.explanation: Integer division counts complete groups. Modulo preserves the items that do not fill another group.

tasks.title: Extract a part name
tasks.prompt: raw contains a part name and may include | followed by a batch code. Take the text before the first |, remove surrounding spaces and convert it to uppercase. Assign it to result.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: The batch code starts after the first delimiter.
Split once, then apply the text methods to the first piece.
tasks.correction: Keep the part name alone. Spaces and later delimiters can vary between inputs.
tasks.solution: result = raw.split('|', 1)[0].strip().upper()
tasks.explanation: Splitting at the first delimiter preserves the whole name. strip and upper give a consistent identifier.

tasks.title: Extend a work list
tasks.prompt: Make a separate working copy of steps and append extra to it. Assign result a dictionary containing original and updated. The original list must keep its earlier values.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: A second variable can still refer to the same list.
Copy the list before appending the new step.
tasks.correction: Appending through another reference changes the original list too. Keep a separate list for the update.
tasks.explanation: copy creates a new outer list. Appending to that copy leaves the original sequence intact.

tasks.title: Count repeated parts
tasks.prompt: Count how often each name appears in parts. Assign result a dictionary from each part name to its count. Preserve repeated observations in the counts.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: Each dictionary key needs one running count.
Start a previously unseen key at zero before adding one.
tasks.correction: A set removes repeats. This task needs the number of observations for each name.
tasks.explanation: The dictionary combines repeated names under one key while retaining their frequencies.

tasks.title: Select hours to total
tasks.prompt: Add only the values in hours that are at least minimum. Assign the total to result. A list with no qualifying values must return zero.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: Test each value before adding it.
Start the running total at zero so an empty selection has a defined result.
tasks.correction: The condition applies to each observation. Keep the qualifying values separate from those below the threshold.
tasks.explanation: The loop adds a value only after its comparison passes. The initial zero also handles an empty selection.

tasks.title: Write a reusable cost function
tasks.prompt: Define job_cost(unit_price, quantity) to return their product. Run and Check call your function with the supplied inputs. The function must return the amount.
tasks.starter: # Define the requested function below.
hints: The caller needs a returned value.
Use the function's parameters rather than numbers from the displayed example.
tasks.correction: Printing an amount leaves the caller without a return value. Compute from the parameters and return the product.
tasks.solution:
def job_cost(unit_price, quantity):
    return unit_price * quantity
tasks.explanation: The checker calls job_cost with each input pair. Returning the product makes the same function usable for other orders.

tasks.title: Read a temporary work note
tasks.prompt: Write text to /tmp/work-note.txt using with. Read it back using with and return it as an integer in result. If the text is not a valid integer, return None.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: Use with around each opened file.
Catch the conversion's ValueError so an invalid observation has an explicit missing result.
tasks.correction: A text value can fail integer conversion. Handle that failure without replacing a valid zero or negative number.
tasks.solution:
with open('/tmp/work-note.txt', 'w') as note:
    note.write(text)
with open('/tmp/work-note.txt') as note:
    raw = note.read()
try:
    result = int(raw)
except ValueError:
    result = None
tasks.explanation: The with blocks close their files. The conversion returns an integer when possible and None for invalid text.

projects.title: Turn readings into tables
projects.description: Shape arrays, inspect CSV data and select the rows a report needs.

tasks.title: Arrange readings into rows
tasks.prompt: Convert readings to a NumPy array. Reshape it using the supplied rows and columns, then assign the array to result. Each case supplies exactly enough readings.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: The dimensions must multiply to the number of readings.
reshape receives the requested row and column counts.
tasks.correction: The requested shape determines where each reading belongs. Preserve the original reading order.
tasks.solution:
import numpy as np
result = np.array(readings).reshape(rows, columns)
tasks.explanation: reshape changes the arrangement of the same values. The number of elements stays constant.

tasks.title: Total each work session
tasks.prompt: Each inner list in sessions holds one session's readings. Use NumPy to total each row and assign the resulting one-dimensional array to result.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: One output belongs to each row.
Summing across columns uses axis=1.
tasks.correction: A single grand total loses the session boundaries. Reduce across each row separately.
tasks.solution:
import numpy as np
result = np.array(sessions).sum(axis=1)
tasks.explanation: axis=1 removes the column dimension, leaving one total per session.

tasks.title: Choose the range endpoints
tasks.prompt: Assign result a dictionary with ticks from NumPy arange(start, stop, step) and samples from linspace(start, stop, count). Keep each function's endpoint rule.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: The two functions describe spacing differently.
arange uses a step and excludes stop. linspace uses a count and includes stop by default.
tasks.correction: Keep the exclusive arange stop separate from linspace's included endpoint.
tasks.solution:
import numpy as np
result = {'ticks': np.arange(start, stop, step), 'samples': np.linspace(start, stop, count)}
tasks.explanation: arange produces step-spaced ticks before stop. linspace spreads the requested number of samples across both endpoints.

tasks.title: Inspect an incoming CSV
tasks.prompt: Read csv_text with pandas and StringIO. Assign the first two rows, with their original columns, to result as a DataFrame.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: StringIO gives the CSV reader a file-like text stream.
head(2) retains up to two rows without changing the column names.
tasks.correction: Use the CSV header as columns. An empty field stays missing, and a short file can contain fewer than two rows.
tasks.solution:
from io import StringIO
import pandas as pd
result = pd.read_csv(StringIO(csv_text)).head(2)
tasks.explanation: read_csv parses the stream into a table. head limits its preview while preserving the data's columns.

tasks.title: Select a label range
tasks.prompt: Build a pandas Series from values with labels as its index. Assign the label slice from first through last, including both labels, to result.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: The endpoints are index labels.
A sorted loc label slice includes its last existing label.
tasks.correction: Positional slicing excludes its stop. This task asks for an inclusive label slice.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
series = pd.Series(values, index=labels)
result = series.loc[first:last]
tasks.explanation: loc uses the supplied labels and includes the two endpoints. The Series result retains their values.

tasks.title: Keep ready estimates
tasks.prompt: Build a DataFrame from jobs. Calculate estimate as hours × rate. Keep ready jobs with estimates at least minimum. Assign columns job and estimate, in original row order, to result.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: Both conditions must pass for the same row.
Parenthesize the comparison before combining it with the Boolean ready column.
tasks.correction: Calculate the estimate from each row, then apply ready and the minimum together. A known zero can qualify.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame(jobs)
df['estimate'] = df['hours'] * df['rate']
result = df.loc[df['ready'] & (df['estimate'] >= minimum), ['job', 'estimate']]
tasks.explanation: The derived column keeps each calculation aligned with its job. The Boolean mask retains only qualifying rows.

projects.title: Build reports you can trust
projects.description: Handle missing observations, check joins and create a revenue report with a visible evidence gap.

tasks.title: Keep unknown hours separate
tasks.prompt: Build a pandas Series from hours. Assign result a dictionary with known for nonmissing count, unknown for missing count and total for the sum of known values. A list containing only missing values has total zero.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: A known zero is still an observation.
count excludes missing values. isna identifies the missing observations.
tasks.correction: Keep missing observations out of known count. Preserve zero and negative values in the known total.
tasks.explanation: The counts retain the denominator information beside the sum. pandas sum returns zero for an all-missing Series by default.

tasks.title: Count usable tags
tasks.prompt: Use a pandas Series to count the nonempty comma-separated tags in each entry of tags. Ignore surrounding spaces and empty pieces. Missing entries have zero tags. Assign the counts to result.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: An empty split piece is not a usable tag.
Test missing values before calling a string method.
tasks.correction: Missing text cannot be split. Filter blank pieces after splitting so extra delimiters do not increase the count.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
series = pd.Series(tags)
result = series.map(lambda value: 0 if pd.isna(value) else len([part for part in value.split(',') if part.strip()]))
tasks.explanation: The transformation handles each entry independently. It counts only pieces that contain text after trimming.

tasks.title: Read calendar years
tasks.prompt: Parse dates as YYYY-MM-DD with pandas. Invalid values become missing. Assign the years as a nullable integer Series to result.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: Make the expected date format explicit.
Coerce invalid dates, then use the datetime accessor for year.
tasks.correction: An invalid calendar date stays missing. Keep it separate from a valid year.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
parsed = pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(dates), format='%Y-%m-%d', errors='coerce')
result = parsed.dt.year.astype('Int64')
tasks.explanation: The explicit format removes date-order guessing. Nullable integer years preserve failed parses.

tasks.title: Summarise department hours
tasks.prompt: Group records by department and sort departments ascending. Return a DataFrame with department, rows, known and total. total must stay missing if a department has no known hours.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: size and count use different denominators.
Require at least one known value when summing each group.
tasks.correction: Report the total row count beside the known-value count. An entirely unknown group has no known total.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame(records, columns=['department', 'hours'])
result = df.groupby('department', sort=True)['hours'].agg(rows='size', known='count', total=lambda x: x.sum(min_count=1)).reset_index()
tasks.explanation: The aggregation keeps row count, available observations and their sum together. min_count=1 preserves an unknown total.

tasks.title: Check a price lookup
tasks.prompt: Left-join jobs to prices on part with many_to_one validation. Return only job and price in job order. If a part appears more than once in prices, return None.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: The lookup should have one row per part.
many_to_one permits repeated parts in jobs and checks uniqueness in prices.
tasks.correction: An unmatched job stays in a left join. Duplicate lookup keys must be detected before they multiply the jobs.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
jobs_df = pd.DataFrame(jobs)
prices_df = pd.DataFrame(prices)
try:
    result = jobs_df.merge(prices_df, on='part', how='left', validate='many_to_one')[['job', 'price']]
except pd.errors.MergeError:
    result = None
tasks.explanation: Relationship validation checks the lookup's key grain. The left join then preserves every job, including unmatched ones.

tasks.title: Lay out shift totals
tasks.prompt: Sum units by area and period. Return a wide DataFrame with area, morning and afternoon, sorted by area. Missing area-period combinations count as zero; units are known counts.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: Repeated area-period observations need aggregation.
Keep both requested period columns even when one has no observations.
tasks.correction: A plain pivot can fail on repeated keys. Sum their known counts and preserve the requested column layout.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame(records, columns=['area', 'period', 'units'])
wide = df.pivot_table(index='area', columns='period', values='units', aggfunc='sum', fill_value=0)
result = wide.reindex(columns=['morning', 'afternoon'], fill_value=0).reset_index()
tasks.explanation: pivot_table combines repeated observations before widening the table. Reindex keeps the two report columns consistent.

tasks.title: Return a report to observations
tasks.prompt: Melt report into columns area, period and units. Keep both morning and afternoon observations, including zeros. Sort by area and then period ascending.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: area identifies the report row.
The period names become values in a new column.
tasks.correction: Preserve both observations for each area. A known zero is part of the data.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame(report, columns=['area', 'morning', 'afternoon'])
result = df.melt(id_vars='area', value_vars=['morning', 'afternoon'], var_name='period', value_name='units').sort_values(['area', 'period']).reset_index(drop=True)
tasks.explanation: melt turns period columns into labelled observations. Sorting defines the requested output order.

tasks.title: Build an auditable revenue report
tasks.prompt: Left-join sales to the unique prices lookup by part. Calculate units × price. Return department, known_revenue and unknown_prices, sorted by department. Keep known_revenue missing when every price in that department is unknown.
tasks.starter:
# Use the supplied input variables.
result = None
hints: Check the price lookup's grain before aggregating.
Track missing prices beside the known revenue instead of turning them into zeros.
tasks.correction: Keep unmatched sales and count their unknown prices. A wholly unknown department needs a missing revenue total.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
sales_df = pd.DataFrame(sales)
prices_df = pd.DataFrame(prices)
joined = sales_df.merge(prices_df, on='part', how='left', validate='many_to_one')
joined['revenue'] = joined['units'] * joined['price']
joined['unknown'] = joined['price'].isna()
result = joined.groupby('department', sort=True).agg(known_revenue=('revenue', lambda x: x.sum(min_count=1)), unknown_prices=('unknown', 'sum')).reset_index()
tasks.explanation: The validated left join preserves sales grain. The report presents the known subtotal beside the amount of missing price evidence.
